Tokyo Blue by Romain Slocombe
Roughly ninety color photographs that explore Tokyo not only as a cityscape but also as a psychological and cultural environment. Rather than presenting tourist imagery, Slocombe focuses on the hidden layers of the metropolis—its nightlife, its intimate interiors, and its underground subcultures.
Inside the book, everyday scenes of Tokyo streets coexist with more intimate or provocative images connected to fetish culture and erotic performance. These photographs reflect Slocombe’s ongoing interest in how private fantasies and social identities intersect with the city’s public spaces.
 The result is a visual narrative that portrays Tokyo as both seductive and enigmatic: a modern metropolis where neon lights, anonymous crowds, and secret desires create a complex cultural landscape.
Published in: 2004;
Condition: Very Good;

Battle royale by Kinji Fukasaki 
Banned in numerous countries due to the extreme violence portrayed, yet it became a cult classic.(being the highest-grossing film in Japan for SIX weeks)
Pioneering the “last-man-standing” genre in film literature, it became the inspiration of many films and videogames of the same genre that were released after it.
Blood, drama, survival and so on, everything encapsulated inside one of the most controversial films at the turn of the new millennium.
Published in: 2000
Condition: Like NEW
NFS.

WHO THE FUCK IS PATRICK CARIOU AS SEEN BY DANNY “BOY” O’CONNOR
One of the most unconventional photobooks ever created, featuring photographs taken by O’Connor in cities such as Los Angeles, Miami, and New York. 
Explicit scenes, public and group sexual activity, drugs, nightlife, tattoos and guns. 
A raw, unfiltered and visceral dive into Patrick Cariou life at the time.
This is not a conventional book — it’s a photographic art project by Danny Boy: a visual tribute or reinterpretation inspired by the work and notoriety of Patrick Cariou, the French photographer known for documenting fringe cultures and for a famous copyright lawsuit involving Richard Prince.
Published in: 2005

Loneliness, longing, unfulfilled love, existential searching and the emptiness of modern life, these are the main themes felt while watching one of the most controversial films debuted at the Cannes Film Festival.
Written, directed, produced, photographed and edited by Vincento Gallo who himself also starred as the main character along with Chloe Sevigny to tell the story of a motorcycle racer on a cross-country drive who is haunted by memories of his former lover.
Gained notoriety at the Cannes Film Festival for its explicit, unconventional sex scene, which sparked debate but also cemented its cult status.
Published in: 2003;
